subject: Next steps: Atlas Health encryption & retention requirements
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: Atlas Health encryption & retention requirements

Thanks again for the call today, Samantha — good to meet you and get a clearer picture of Atlas Health's requirements. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before Marissa and Dev draft the technical proposal.

Summary of what I captured (please flag anything I missed):
- Data types: PHI + PII in prompts and outputs; patient identifiers (MRN), appointment data, and some provider notes.
- Residency: Primary processing must occur in US regions; a subset of records for clinical trials may need EU-only residency (we noted possible narrow-scope exceptions).
- Retention: Audit and access logs: 7 years (per internal legal), PII payloads: configured retention policy (starts at 3 years but needs legal sign-off).
- Encryption: In-transit TLS 1.2+ required; at-rest AES-256 standard. Customer wants customer-managed keys (BYOK/CMEK) with HSM-backed key storage (FIPS 140-2/3 output desired).
- Logging: Immutable audit trails for admin activity, key operations logs (KMS request metadata), and per-request token-level usage logs (retention/aggregation options discussed).

Proposed next steps (owners and dates):
1) Redwood to send an architecture sketch showing BYOK/CMEK integration options (Karthik / Marissa) — target Tue 05/25.
2) Dev to check compatibility matrix for HSM providers we support (AWS CloudHSM, Azure Key Vault HSM, on-prem HSM via PKCS#11 gateway) and note any limitations for our Dedicated/Private offerings (Dev) — target Wed 05/26.
3) Samantha to confirm final retention targets for PII vs. logs (Atlas legal) — target Fri 05/28.
4) Exchange sample audit log schema and retention SLAs; Redwood to include expected fields and storage durations in the proposal (Marissa) — target Wed 05/26.

Attachments: I pushed our PII data map template and a short PDF summarizing Redwood's KMS options (attached).

If this alignment looks right, Marissa will produce the proposal and a recommended deployment path (Hosted with Dedicated-backed keys vs Private deployment with customer HSM gateway) based on your final retention/residency choices.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: PII-data-map.xlsx (spreadsheet)
Attachment: redwood-kms-options.pdf (one-page summary)
From: Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@atlashealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Atlas Health - Security Team <security@atlashealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: Atlas Health encryption & retention requirements

Karthik — thanks for the concise recap. A few clarifications from legal/security after the internal sync: 
- Retention: Legal is pushing for 7 years for audit logs; PII payload retention is more nuanced — they want the ability to configure per-data-class retention (minimum 3 years, maximum policy 7 years). We need support for configurable retention by label/class.
- Keys: BYOK is preferred. We will insist on HSM-protected keys (FIPS 140-2 Level 3 would be ideal). If Redwood offers a Cloud KMS integration, it must support customer-owned keys with key rotation logs exported.
- Residency: Confirmed — primary infra must be in US regions for PHI. A small subset (clinical trial cohort) will be EU-only; we will identify the records and the trigger for EU routing.
- Logging: We need tamper-evident audit logs for admin actions and key usage events. A weekly digest to our SIEM (Splunk) via secure forwarding is requested.

Questions for Redwood: 
1) Does Redwood support HSM-backed CMEK where we control key import/rotation?
2) Can audit logs be retained separately from payload retention and exported to our S3 (or equivalent) with lifecycle rules?
3) What are the latency implications for using Dedicated with a remote HSM (e.g., CloudHSM in a different AZ)?

I'll aim to confirm the final retention matrix by Friday. We appreciate the architecture sketch.

— Samantha
Director, InfoSec | Atlas Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@atlashealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: Atlas Health encryption & retention requirements

Samantha — thanks for the clarifications, helpful. Karthik and I had a quick internal sync; below is a proposed scope for the formal proposal and the items we'll enumerate in the architecture doc. We'll also call out tradeoffs so legal can see the choices.

Planned contents of our proposal (deliverable targeted Wed 05/26):
- Executive summary: recommended deployment modes (Hosted + Dedicated with CMEK OR Private deployment with HSM gateway).
- KMS options and mechanics:
  - Cloud CMEK: integrate with AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault (customer key ownership where supported), pros/cons.
  - HSM gateway (on-prem or partner-hosted): PKCS#11 bridge model, how we mount keys for signing/encryption operations without exposing raw key material.
  - Bring-your-own-key import vs. external key references (we'll map which options allow importable keys vs. key-wrapping).
- Audit & logging plan:
  - Log schema sample (attached sample).
  - Retention controls: per-data-class lifecycle policies, export hooks to your SIEM/S3, and tamper-evidence checks (immutable storage options / object lock).
- Residency & routing: config knobs for EU-only cohorts and failover behavior.
- Performance and latency: expected token latency delta for CMEK vs Redwood-managed keys and for remote HSM calls; preliminary numbers and caveats.
- Implementation plan & owner matrix: who does key provisioning, connector config, and verification steps (we'll surface required access).

Action owners we assigned:
- Dev: run a quick lab to quantify round-trip latency to CloudHSM per AZ and surface any SDK limitations.
- Marissa: assemble proposal doc and sample log schema (will include attachment audit-log-sample.txt).
- Karthik: coordinate with your legal for final retention matrix and confirm contact for SIEM ingestion.

We attached the sample log schema and a PII mapping template to help you fill in the retention matrix. If you can share the completed PII-data-map.xlsx by Friday, we should be able to finalize the pricing/ops annex and present a recommended path for production within two weeks.

Marissa Cole
Manager, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: audit-log-sample.txt (log schema example)
From: Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@atlashealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: Atlas Health encryption & retention requirements

Thanks Marissa — that scope looks good. I'll get the PII-data-map back to you by EOD Friday and loop in our Cloud Architect on the SIEM forwarding details. For question 1: we'll push for FIPS 140-2 Level 3 HSM; if Redwood can show a design that meets that bar (or a supported partner), that will accelerate procurement.

Samantha
Director, InfoSec | Atlas Health
